headline: Opus 5 leads SWE-bench Pro with 79.2% against GPT-5.6 Sol and Kimi K3
summary: Anthropic's Opus 5 takes the lead in critical coding benchmarks like SWE-bench Pro, while OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol excels in agentic terminal tasks. Moonshot's Kimi K3 offers a powerful open-weight alternative.
details: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol, and Moonshot's Kimi K3 all shipped within a 15-day window in July, setting a new competitive landscape for flagship AI models. Opus 5 currently leads SWE-bench Pro with 79.2% accuracy, significantly outperforming Sol's 64.6%.

Opus 5 also shows a strong lead in ARC-AGI-3, scoring 30.2 against Sol's 7.8, though this gap warrants independent replication due to potential training-set contamination. For multi-step tool use, Opus 5 has a 26% relative lead on Frontier-Bench v0.1.

GPT-5.6 Sol, however, holds the top spot on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with 91.9% in its top mode, an industry-leading figure for agentic terminal performance. It also excels in DeepSWE 1.1 and HealthBench Professional.

Moonshot's Kimi K3 is a 2.8 trillion parameter open-weight model, priced competitively at 3 and 15 per million tokens, roughly 40% under Opus 5 for input. Its Mixture-of-Experts architecture activates 16 out of 896 subnetworks per token, allowing for efficient scaling.

All three models now feature context windows at or above a million tokens and output caps around 128k, making these once-headline features standard. The key differentiators have shifted to their behavioral performance under complex agentic loads.

It's crucial to note that GPT-5.6 Sol was generally available on July 9 after a June 26 preview, and it's part of a three-model family (Terra, Luna, Sol). Comparisons should specify the exact tier of GPT-5.6 to avoid misleading results.

Independent analyses, such as Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, provide a neutral perspective. This index places GPT-5.6 Sol at 59, significantly above the median for similar reasoning models, highlighting its strong general intelligence.

The separation between models is most pronounced in agent loop workloads, where models must plan, execute, debug, and iterate. This is where Opus 5's strong coding benchmarks become particularly relevant.

headline_marked: [[Galaxy Z Flip 8's Flex Window]] gains Quick Settings and App Tray access
headline: Galaxy Z Flip 8's Flex Window gains Quick Settings and App Tray access
summary: Samsung's new Galaxy Z Flip 8 significantly upgrades its outer Flex Window, allowing users to access Quick Settings and an App Tray without unfolding the device. This enhances convenience and reduces wear on the main display.
details: The Samsung Galaxy Z Flip 8 introduces a major upgrade to its outer display, now called the Flex Window. This redesigned screen finally provides direct access to Quick Settings and an App Tray, making the clamshell phone far more functional when closed.

While core specs like the 50MP/12MP camera, display size, and battery remain similar to its predecessor, the Z Flip 8 is smaller, lighter, and more durable. It also features Horizon Lock, a new super stabilization camera feature for video recording.

The enhanced Flex Window optimizes popular apps to work better on the smaller screen, displaying recents and automations. Samsung's Now Brief has also been upgraded to fit more tools and information, with customizable cards for personalized use.

Users can now perform common tasks like disconnecting Bluetooth devices, enabling Do Not Disturb, or activating a mobile hotspot directly from the cover screen. This eliminates the need to constantly open the phone for frequent setting changes.

This upgrade mirrors the quick access appeal of smartwatches, allowing users to manage music, notifications, and other functions without fully engaging the main display. It also helps preserve the foldable screen's lifespan by reducing unnecessary flexing.
